name: Sahel insurgency
summary: JNIM insurgency persists in Mali, but Bamako's fuel supply has been restored under escort
state: Mali's government had restored fuel supplies to Bamako by September, with more than 900 tankers entering under military escort by 14 Sep, though armed groups can still disrupt key routes (Al Jazeera, 22 Sep). Human Rights Watch documented continued JNIM and army abuses through September (19 Oct). With no current blockade of the capital confirmed, Alert is not supported; rated Watch as of 4 Nov.
for_you: FCDO advises against all travel to Mali and much of the Sahel. Coastal West African states near the border also carry warnings.
rubric_hit: Sustained insurgency at current levels = Watch; no confirmed blockade of a capital

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Mali marks independence amid a worsening security crisis
Human Rights Watch — Mali: military attacks on civilians, insurgent abuses

why: Jihadist groups control growing territory across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, driving displacement and coastal-state spillover.
drivers: JNIM/IS-Sahel offensives, juntas, Russian forces, blockades, coastal-state attacks.

rubric.alert: Blockade or fall of a capital or major city, or mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states.
